name: Equal-highs / equal-lows liquidity sweep: fade a wick through a stacked pool that closes back inside (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. POOL (highs): among swing highs with bar index j in [i-120, i-3], take a candidate level L = high[j]; its members are all such swing highs with high within [L-0.15A, L]; the pool is valid if it has >= 2 members and NO bar since the latest member's index and before bar i has high > L (unswept). Choose the valid pool with the largest L. ENTER short at close[i] if high[i] > L+0.05A and close[i] < L, with stop = high[i], R = stop - close[i] in [0.3A, 3A]. LOWS mirrored: pool of >=2 swing lows within [L, L+0.15A], smallest L, ENTER long if low[i] < L-0.05A and close[i] > L, stop = low[i]. If both sides qualify on one bar, skip. EXIT on close beyond the stop, on close at or past entry -/+ 2R, or after 24 bars.
rationale: TJR and ICT argue that equal highs/lows carry double the resting orders (stops plus breakout entries) and are the preferred sweep targets. The registry tests single-level sweeps (previous-day and Asia), never the stacked-pool version.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 5 (equal highs/lows, youtu.be/AGmAVyAuBE0 @ 00:38:28); Osler 2003, 'Currency orders and exchange rate dynamics: an explanation for the predictive success of technical analysis', Journal of Finance 58(5), 1791-1819

name: Core TJR model, step 1-2: swing-high sweep confirmed by a break of structure, target the prior liquidity draw (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. SHORT: a sweep bar s has high[s] > H*+0.05A where H* is the swing high at index j (known at s). Pullback low Lm = lowest low over bars j..s-1 (require s-j <= 60). Within bars s..s+12, the first bar c with close[c] < Lm is the BOS (body close; a wick does not count); track sweepHigh = max high over bars s..c. ENTER short at close[c] with stop = sweepHigh, R = stop-close[c] in [0.5A, 4A]. Target Lt = lowest low over the 48 bars before s; skip if close[c]-Lt < 1.0R. EXIT when close >= stop, close <= Lt, or after 48 bars. A new sweep during the confirm window restarts the window from the new sweep bar (extend sweepHigh). LONG mirrored (sweep of L*, BOS = close above the pullback high Hm, target the highest high of the 48 bars before s). Setups are armed only when flat.
rationale: This is TJR's stated primary model (potential = sweep, confirmation = BOS, exit at the next draw on liquidity). The registry's t100-bos-h tests plain HH/HL structure, not sweep-then-BOS with a liquidity-draw exit.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 9.1 (youtu.be/xRuMUvW3T7Q, youtu.be/TEp3a-7GUds); section 6 (body-close BOS, youtu.be/Zzk864cVJek)

name: Core TJR model, iFVG confirmation: sweep of a swing high, then a close through the outer edge of the bullish FVG stack (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. FVG: bullish FVG completed at bar c (middle bar m=c-1) if low[c] > high[m-1] and close[m] > open[m] and low[c]-high[m-1] >= 0.3A(c); zone = [high[m-1], low[c]]. SHORT: sweep bar s as in rule of c1031-tjr-02 (high[s] > H*+0.05A). STACK = all bullish FVGs completed in bars [s-8, s] that have no close below their lower edge up to bar s; require >= 1; stackBottom = min lower edge. The iFVG confirmation is the first bar c2 in (s, s+12] with close[c2] < stackBottom. ENTER short at close[c2], stop = max(high over bars s..c2), R in [0.5A, 4A]; target Lt = lowest low over the 48 bars before s, skip if close[c2]-Lt < 1.0R. EXIT when close >= stop, close <= Lt, or after 48 bars. LONG mirrored (sweep of L*, bearish FVG stack, close above stackTop, target highest high of 48 bars before s).
rationale: TJR weights an inverse FVG equal to a BOS and says it often fires earlier, giving better R:R. This tests that claim as a confirmation rule against the BOS version (c1031-tjr-02) on the same sweeps.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 7 (iFVG, youtu.be/4sRDnVmLcMk @ 00:10:42, outermost-gap rule @ 00:16:37)

name: Core TJR model, step 3: after sweep + BOS, enter the first rejection of the 50% equilibrium of the displacement leg (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. SHORT: detect sweep s and BOS bar c exactly as in c1031-tjr-02 (do NOT enter at c). Leg top = max high over s..c; leg bottom = min low over bars s..c; EQ = (top+bottom)/2. Within bars c+1..c+24 the first bar r with high[r] >= EQ and close[r] < EQ is the reaction: ENTER short at close[r], stop = top, R = top-close[r] in [0.5A, 6A]; target Lt = lowest low over the 48 bars before s; skip if close[r]-Lt < 1.0R. Cancel the setup if any close in c+1..r-1 exceeds top, or if no reaction by c+24. EXIT when close >= top, close <= Lt, or 48 bars after entry. LONG mirrored.
rationale: TJR's step 3 is not to chase the BOS but to wait for a retrace to equilibrium and a reaction. Compared with c1031-tjr-02 it tests whether waiting for the pullback helps net of the trades it misses.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 9.1, section 7 (equilibrium, youtu.be/TEp3a-7GUds @ 00:32:03)

name: NY-open sweep of the London range: fade a wick through the London high/low that closes back inside, hold to 16:00 New York (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. NYH (hour of the US cash open bar) = 13 if the bar's UTC calendar day D satisfies secondSundayOfMarch(year) <= D < firstSundayOfNovember(year) (US daylight time), else 14; the bar with hour NYH contains 09:30 New York time; 'NY flat bar' = the bar with hour NYH+6 (its close is 16:00 New York). For UTC day D, LONDON range = max high / min low over the 1h bars with hour 7..NYH-1 of day D (all must exist). At the NY open bar N (hour == NYH): if high[N] > londonHigh+0.05A and close[N] < londonHigh then SHORT; if low[N] < londonLow-0.05A and close[N] > londonLow then LONG; if both, skip. ENTER at close[N]; stop = high[N] (short) / low[N] (long); target = londonLow (short) / londonHigh (long); skip if (distance to target) < 1.0 x R. EXIT when close hits stop or target, else flat at the NY flat bar close. At most one trade per UTC day per asset.
rationale: TJR trades the NY open as the manipulation window that sweeps pre-market (London) liquidity before the real move. The registry has Asia-range sweeps in London and an ORB, but never the London range swept at the NY open. Adjacent: c1031-intraday-29 (cash-open spike fade) uses a spike, not a session-range sweep.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 8 (9:30 open routine, youtu.be/L4xz2o23aPQ) and section 5 (session highs/lows)

NYH (hour of the US cash open bar) = 13 if the bar's UTC calendar day D satisfies secondSundayOfMarch(year) <= D < firstSundayOfNovember(year) (US daylight time), else 14; the bar with hour NYH contains 09:30 New York time; 'NY flat bar' = the bar with hour NYH+6 (its close is 16:00 New York). LONDON range as in c1031-tjr-05. At the NY open bar N (hour == NYH): if close[N] > londonHigh+0.25A then LONG; if close[N] < londonLow-0.25A then SHORT; else no trade. ENTER at close[N]. rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. Week = Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 UTC; PWH / PWL = high / low of the completed previous week (needs all 168 bars). SHORT: in the current week the first bar s with high[s] > PWH+0.05A and close[s] < PWH (first sweep of PWH this week). BOS level = lowest low over bars s-6..s. The first bar c in (s, s+12] with close[c] < BOS level is the confirmation: ENTER short at close[c], stop = max high over s..c, R in [0.5A, 8A]; target = low of the UTC day before the day containing s (previous daily low from before the sweep); skip if close[c]-target < 1.0R. EXIT on close >= stop, close <= target, or after 120 bars. LONG mirrored with PWL, and the previous daily HIGH as target. One trade per side per week.
rationale: TJR's weekly-range liquidity swing: sweep the prior week's extreme, require a 1H BOS, single TP at the prior daily extreme. He says forex/gold only; this asks whether it transfers to crypto. Adjacent: c1031-intraday-09 breaks the prior-week level as continuation.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 9.4 (youtu.be/_4-gzk18pQw @ 00:11:08)

name: Premium/discount continuation: 4H HH/HL or LH/LL bias, enter the first 1h rejection of the 50% equilibrium of the last 4H leg (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. BIAS4H: build 4H bars by grouping 1h bars on floor(time/14400), a 4H bar is complete once its 4th hour has closed; apply SWING (k=2) to complete 4H bars (a 4H swing is known only after two later complete 4H bars); bias = +1 if the last two confirmed 4H swing highs are rising AND the last two confirmed 4H swing lows are rising, -1 if both are falling, else 0. LONG when BIAS4H == +1: SH = latest confirmed 4H swing high, legLow = the confirmed 4H swing low that immediately precedes SH in time (require one to exist); EQ = (SH+legLow)/2. ENTER long at close[i] if low[i] <= EQ and close[i] > EQ and close[i] < SH, stop = legLow, R = close[i]-legLow in [0.5A, 8A]; target = SH. Cancel (no entries on this leg) once any 1h close is below legLow. SHORT when BIAS4H == -1, mirrored (legHigh preceding the latest 4H swing low SL, EQ in the middle, enter if high[i] >= EQ and close[i] < EQ and close[i] > SL, target SL). EXIT on close at or beyond stop or target, or after 72 bars. Recompute the leg each bar; once in a position keep the stored stop/target.
rationale: TJR's premium/discount filter run on the 4H chart: buy discount in an uptrend, sell premium in a downtrend, and wait for a reaction at 50%. Adjacent but distinct: c1031-intraday-31 uses a fixed 168-hour Fibonacci 61.8% rule with no structure bias.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 4 (premium/discount filter, youtu.be/Qk-mHUlSJGU @ 00:16:35) and section 7 (equilibrium)

name: Stacked-liquidity run: a body close through a stack of 3+ swing lows (or highs) continues, 'cookies in the jar' (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. POOL (lows): among swing lows with index j in [i-168, i-3], candidate level L = low[j]; members = swing lows with low within [L, L+0.5A]; valid if >= 3 members and no bar since the earliest member has low < L (unswept). Choose the valid pool with the smallest L. SHORT when close[i] < L-0.2A and close[i-1] >= L: ENTER short at close[i]; stop level = L+1.0A (so R = L+1.0A-close[i]); target = close[i] - 2R. POOL (highs) mirrored (>= 3 swing highs within [L-0.5A, L], largest L), LONG when close[i] > L+0.2A and close[i-1] <= L, stop level L-1.0A. If both sides qualify, skip. EXIT on close beyond the stop level, close at or past the target, or after 24 bars.
rationale: TJR says a stack of unswept lows/highs gets 'blitzed' once price starts breaking through, because each level holds resting orders. This is the continuation counterpart to c1031-tjr-01 (reversal at an equal-level wick): a body close through the stack versus a wick through it.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 5 (low-resistance liquidity, youtu.be/AGmAVyAuBE0 @ 00:27:16 and 00:29:18)

name: Nearest unswept draw on liquidity: each UTC day, trade toward the nearer untouched swing high/low (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. Decide only on the bar with hour == 23 (its close is the UTC day boundary); otherwise, if already in a position, apply EXIT. UNSWEPT set: swing highs / lows with index in [i-168, i-3] such that no later bar through bar i has high >= the swing high (low <= the swing low). HU = lowest unswept swing high above close[i]; LD = highest unswept swing low below close[i]; require both to exist. dU = (HU-close[i])/A, dD = (close[i]-LD)/A. dNear = min(dU,dD); require 0.5 <= dNear <= 5. ENTER long if dU < dD (toward HU), short if dD < dU (toward LD); skip ties. EXIT: close reaches the target level (close >= HU long / close <= LD short), or close moves against entry by 2 x dNear x A (disaster stop), or after 24 bars.
rationale: TJR's top-down bias: mark the draws on liquidity and lean toward the stronger unswept one. The mechanical proxy is the nearest untouched swing extreme. A pure test of the 'price is drawn to resting orders' premise with no sweep or confirmation attached.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 4 (daily bias, youtu.be/ox3p5Um1TqY) and section 5 (draws on liquidity, youtu.be/TEp3a-7GUds @ 00:22:23); Osler 2003, 'Currency orders and exchange rate dynamics: an explanation for the predictive success of technical analysis', Journal of Finance 58(5), 1791-1819

name: Standalone inverse FVG: a close through the outer edge of a recent FVG stack flips the gap into a reversal signal (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. FVG as defined in c1031-tjr-03 (bullish: low[c] > high[c-2] and close[c-1] > open[c-1], gap >= 0.3A(c), zone [high[c-2], low[c]]; bearish mirrored: high[c] < low[c-2], close[c-1] < open[c-1], zone [high[c], low[c-2]]). ACTIVE bullish FVGs at bar i = those completed in bars [i-48, i-1] with no close below their lower edge through bar i-1. If >= 1 active, stackBottom = min lower edge, stackTop = max upper edge. SHORT when close[i] < stackBottom: ENTER at close[i], stop = stackTop, R = stackTop-close[i] in [0.3A, 4A] (otherwise discard the stack permanently); target = close[i]-2R. LONG mirrored (active bearish FVGs, close[i] > max upper edge, stop = min lower edge). If both sides trigger, skip. EXIT on close beyond the stop, close at or past the target, or after 24 bars.
rationale: TJR calls an inverse FVG a reversal/confirmation signal equal to a BOS. The registry tests the FVG retest (t100-fvg-h) as continuation; the inversion event itself, with no sweep requirement, is untested.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 7 (iFVG, youtu.be/4sRDnVmLcMk; youtu.be/xcDOMKaOIsk @ 00:28:03)

name: Balanced price range: first return into the overlap of two opposite FVGs, trade in the direction of the later gap (crypto 1h)
rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. FVG definition as in c1031-tjr-11 with minimum width 0.2A. BPR forms at bar t when an FVG of one type completes at t and an opposite-type FVG completed at t1 in [t-30, t-2] with zone overlap ovLo = max(lo1,lo2), ovHi = min(hi1,hi2), ovHi-ovLo >= 0.2A. Direction = type of the later gap (bullish later gap -> LONG). LONG entry: the first bar i in (t, t+48] with low[i] <= ovHi and close[i] > ovLo: ENTER long at close[i], stop = min(lo1, lo2), R in [0.3A, 4A], target = close+2R. Cancel the BPR if a close in (t, i) is below ovLo (long) / above ovHi (short). SHORT mirrored (bearish later gap, entry when high[i] >= ovLo and close[i] < ovHi, stop = max(hi1, hi2)). EXIT on close beyond the stop, close at or past the target, or after 48 bars. Ignore new BPRs while in a position.
rationale: A BPR is the ICT/TJR imbalance-rebalance zone; TJR found it independently and says price rips back through it. It is the only imbalance concept in the dossier that the registry has not touched.

LONG if low[i] < m-0.05A and close[i] > m and oiChg <= -0.01 (a stop run under the 48h low during which open interest fell >= 1% in 3 hours: positions were force-closed); stop = low[i], R = close-low[i] in [0.3A, 4A], target = close+2R. rule: Conventions (1h crypto, UTC): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); hour = floor(time/3600)%24, day = floor(time/86400), dow = (day+3)%7 with Monday = 0; stops and targets are tested on bar CLOSES only (no intrabar fills; if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. BIAS4H: build 4H bars by grouping 1h bars on floor(time/14400), a 4H bar is complete once its 4th hour has closed; apply SWING (k=2) to complete 4H bars (a 4H swing is known only after two later complete 4H bars); bias = +1 if the last two confirmed 4H swing highs are rising AND the last two confirmed 4H swing lows are rising, -1 if both are falling, else 0. LONG when BIAS4H == +1: bar i has low[i] < L*-0.05A and close[i] > L* (a 1h swing low swept with a close back above): ENTER long at close[i], stop = low[i], R in [0.3A, 4A]; target = the latest confirmed 4H swing high (must be above close[i] by >= 1.5R, else skip). SHORT when BIAS4H == -1: high[i] > H*+0.05A and close[i] < H*, stop = high[i], target = the latest confirmed 4H swing low, same 1.5R rule. No trades when BIAS4H == 0 and none against the bias. EXIT on close beyond the stop, at or past the target, or after 72 bars.
rationale: TJR calls 'never trade against HTF bias' close to an absolute rule. This is the cleanest test of that rule: the same 1h sweep-and-close pattern, taken only with the 4H structure. The single-level fades already in the registry (previous-day, Asia) take both directions.

name: Daily premium/discount continuation: HH/HL or LH/LL structure, enter the first rejection of the 50% of the last swing leg (ETF 1d)
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. STRUCTURE: UP if the last two confirmed swing highs are rising AND the last two confirmed swing lows are rising; DOWN if both falling; else none. rationale: Daily-timeframe version of c1031-tjr-08 on ETFs (TJR's bias check is the 4H; the daily is the swing-trader variant). Tests whether 50%-of-leg entries add anything to trading with structure on slower assets.

name: Weekly BOS, daily retrace: after a weekly body-close break of structure, enter the first daily rejection of the 50% of the leg (ETF 1d)
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. WEEKLY bars W from ctx.resample(bars[0..i],'1w'), using only COMPLETE weekly bars. Weekly swing (k=2) is confirmed two weeks later. BOS-up at completed week w: close_w > SHw (the last confirmed weekly swing high as of week w) and close_{w-1} <= SHw. legLow = lowest weekly low between the swing-high week and w inclusive; legHigh = max high of all daily bars from the start of week w to the current bar i (running). EQ = (legLow+legHigh)/2. LONG: during the 30 trading days after week w completes, the first daily bar i with low[i] <= EQ and close[i] > EQ: ENTER long at close[i], stop: exit when close < legLow, target: exit when close >= legHigh at entry; EXIT after 60 bars. BOS-down mirrored (close_w < last weekly swing low, SHORT on the first daily bar with high >= EQ and close < EQ). A new BOS replaces an unused one. Only one position per ETF.
rationale: TJR's multi-timeframe cascade: a BOS on one timeframe is a retracement of the next higher timeframe and the lower timeframe provides the entry. Weekly BOS + daily entry is the swing-trader rung of that chain.

name: Monthly break of structure, hold until the prior high is reclaimed and a weekly BOS down (ETF 1d), TJR's long-term investment model
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. MONTHLY bars from ctx.resample(bars[0..i],'1M') using only COMPLETE months; monthly swing with k=1 (high[j] > high of months j-1 and j+1), known one month later. BOS-up at completed month m: close_m > SHm (last confirmed monthly swing high as of month m) and close_{m-1} <= SHm. T = max(SHm, max monthly high of the 12 months before m); legLow = lowest monthly low from the swing-high month to m. ENTER long at the close of the first trading day after month m completes. Stage1 is reached at the first daily close >= T. EXIT (a) before stage 1: close < legLow; (b) after stage 1: a completed weekly close below the last confirmed weekly swing low (k=2 weekly) -- a weekly BOS down BEFORE stage 1 is ignored; (c) after 756 bars. Long only. Ignore new BOS while in a position.
rationale: TJR's 'lying around money' model (monthly BOS entry, no dip-buying, hold until the swing high is reclaimed and a weekly BOS ends it). The dossier's 4,400% BTC example is unaudited; this tests the rule on 25 ETFs. The text of the exit is ambiguous, so the prior-high reading (T above) is fixed here before any run.

rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. rationale: TJR refines the monthly-BOS entry with a weekly retest near equilibrium, 'explicitly rejecting buying the dip'. This asks whether waiting for the retest beats the immediate entry (c1031-tjr-25), on a stock universe. Survivorship-biased large caps, disclosed.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 9.6 (youtu.be/8IyR7pAvamE)

name: Dual-index structure alignment: hold QQQ+DIA only while both show HH/HL structure (ETF 1d, TJR's ES/NQ gate)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode on the two-asset universe, rebalance daily, weights >= 0 summing <= 1, missing = 0; uses only bars up to the rebalance close. For each sym in {QQQ, DIA}: confirmed daily swings (k=2: high[j] strictly above the highs of j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2; known from the close of j+2; swing low mirrored); state(sym) = UP if the last two confirmed swing highs are rising AND the last two confirmed swing lows are rising, otherwise NOT-UP (needs >= 2 of each, else NOT-UP). If both QQQ and DIA are UP, return {QQQ: 0.5, DIA: 0.5}; otherwise return {} (cash). A session with only one of the two symbols present returns {}.
rationale: TJR's 2026 rule: never trade unless ES and NQ agree on bias; if the indices are not aligned, call it a day. The daily proxy asks whether structure agreement across two US index ETFs improves on being long always. QQQ/DIA stand in for NQ/ES (no futures data; SPY is holdout).
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 9.1 (dual-index gate, youtu.be/8PYgFVB0GHE @ 00:49:07 and 00:53:27)

name: Failed break of structure trap on large caps: a body close beyond the swing point lost within 3 days (US stocks 1d)
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. SHORT: BOS bar b is the first bar with close[b] > H*+0.1A and close[b-1] <= H*. The first bar c in (b, b+3] with close[c] < H* is the trap: ENTER short at close[c], stop = max high over b..c, R in [0.3A, 4A], target = close-2R. LONG mirrored (close below L*-0.1A, then back above L* within 3 bars; stop = min low over b..c). EXIT on close beyond the stop, at or past the target, or after 15 bars. Shorts pay no borrow in the harness (disclosed).
rationale: Second market for c1031-tjr-13 (daily large caps with a long bias). The bear-trap (long) side is the more likely edge on a rising universe; both sides are fixed in advance so the comparison cannot be tuned.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 6 (BOS vs fake-out) and section 5 (sweep vs break)

name: Previous-month high/low sweep: first daily close back inside after a wick through last month's extreme, target last month's midpoint (ETF 1d)
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. For the current calendar month (UTC date of the bar), PMH / PML / PMmid = high / low / midpoint over all daily bars of the previous calendar month (needs >= 15 bars). SHORT on the first bar i of the current month with high[i] > PMH+0.05A and close[i] < PMH, provided no earlier bar this month closed above PMH: ENTER at close[i], stop = high[i], target = PMmid; skip if close[i]-PMmid < 1.0 x (high[i]-close[i]). LONG mirrored with PML (low[i] < PML-0.05A, close[i] > PML, no earlier close below PML this month, stop = low[i], target PMmid). EXIT on close beyond the stop, at/past the target, or after 20 bars. At most one trade per side per month per ETF.
rationale: TJR/ICT list previous-month and higher-timeframe highs/lows as liquidity draws. The registry has 20-day and previous-day sweeps but no calendar-month level.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 5 (session/HTF highs-lows); Osler 2003, 'Currency orders and exchange rate dynamics: an explanation for the predictive success of technical analysis', Journal of Finance 58(5), 1791-1819

name: Daily order block after a body-close BOS: retest of the last down candle before the displacement leg (ETF 1d)
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. BULLISH: BOS bar b: close[b] > H* and close[b-1] <= H* (H* known at b) and close[b]-open[b] >= 1.0A. OB = the last bar j in [b-5, b-1] with close[j] < open[j] (none -> skip); zone [low[j], high[j]]. During bars b+1..b+25, ENTER long at close[i] on the first bar with low[i] <= high[j] and close[i] > low[j]; cancel the OB if any close in (b, i) is below low[j]. stop = low[j], R = close-low[j] in [0.3A, 4A], target = close+2R. BEARISH mirrored (close[b] < L*, up-candle OB, zone [low[j], high[j]], SHORT when high[i] >= low[j] and close[i] < high[j], stop = high[j]). EXIT on close beyond the stop, at/past the target, or after 20 bars.
rationale: TJR named order blocks as his #1 retracement entry, then partly dropped them. t100-ob-h tests an ATR-impulse zone on hourly crypto; this uses a BOS-validated zone on a different market and timeframe (daily ETFs), so it is a new instance, not a re-run.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 7 (order blocks, youtu.be/qhuFg_OXdmE @ 00:03:07 and 00:06:48; dropped-then-reused, youtu.be/wzq2AMsoJKY)

name: Monthly-open Judas swing: with last month's bias, buy the first reclaim of the month's open after an early-month dip (ETF 1d)
rule: Conventions (1d): signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; decisions are made on the close of bar i and fill no earlier than bar i+1; return +1/-1 while a position is open, else 0 (longShort true); one position per asset, new setups are ignored while a position is open; A = ctx.atr(14) at bar i (no signal while NaN); stops and targets are tested on daily CLOSES only (if stop and target both qualify on one close, stop wins); R = |entry close - stop|; a setup whose R falls outside its stated band is skipped, not resized; SWING (k=2): bar j is a swing high if high[j] > high of bars j-2, j-1, j+1, j+2 (strict), known only from the close of bar j+2; swing low mirrored with low; H* / L* = the most recent confirmed swing high / low as of bar i. Month boundary: bar i is trading day 1 of a month when its UTC calendar month differs from bar i-1's; k = trading-day number within the month. MonthOpen = open of day 1. Bias from the previous complete month: LONG bias if its close > its open (first-day open to last-day close) and its close >= its low + 0.5 x (high-low); SHORT bias if close < open and close <= low + 0.5 x (high-low); else none. LONG: ARM at the first day a (k <= 10) with close[a] < MonthOpen-0.5A; the first later day c (k <= 15) with close[c] > MonthOpen is the confirmation: ENTER long at close[c], stop S = min low over a..c (exit if a later close < S); target = previous month high PMH: skip if PMH-close[c] < 1.0 x (close[c]-S). SHORT mirrored (ARM close > MonthOpen+0.5A, confirm close < MonthOpen, stop = max high a..c, target PML). EXIT on stop, at/past the target, or after 15 bars. One trade per month per ETF.
rationale: The ICT monthly-open Judas swing: a false early-month move against the monthly bias, then a reversal. The weekly-open version failed in the registry (c1023-pop-32 on hourly crypto); the monthly-open on ETFs is a different market and level, with bias fixed from the prior month.
source: research/TJR-trading-research.md section 8 and section 4 (bias, manipulation window); ICT monthly/weekly/daily open teaching material
